claim: The experiment studies rearranging regions in slow athermal flow by observing a concentrated oil-in-water emulsion flowing in a thin chamber with a constricting hopper shape.
quote: observing the flow of a concentrated oil-in-water emulsion in a thin chamber

claim: The sample chamber gap is 0.10 ± 0.02 mm, controlled by a thin film of double-sided adhesive tape sandwiched between two glass plates.
quote: The sample chamber has a gap of $0.10 \pm 0.02$ mm

claim: The droplets are silicone oil (poly-dimethylsiloxane, ρ = 1 g/mL, η = 350 mPa·s) in water, made by the co-flow microfluidic technique and stabilized by Fairy soap at mass fraction 0.025.
quote: made by the “co-flow” microfluidic technique

claim: The droplets have a diameter at least twice the gap thickness, so they are compressed into quasi-two-dimensional pancake shapes.
quote: diameter at least twice as large as the gap thickness

claim: The samples have area fraction φ ≥ 0.90 and are jammed (jamming point φJ ≈ 0.84), so a finite nonzero stress is required for flow.
quote: area fraction $\phi \geqslant 0.90$ , at which the samples are jammed

claim: A T1 event is a localized plastic rearrangement defined as a topological change where four droplets exchange neighbors.
quote: a topological change of four droplets exchanging neighbors

claim: Droplet deformation D is quantified as the standard deviation of the radius r(θ), with the perimeter discretized at 200 evenly spaced angles.
quote: discretize the perimeter at 200 evenly spaced angles

claim: Nearest neighbors are determined using the Laguerre (radical) tessellation, chosen because the samples are polydisperse.
quote: Laguerre (radical) tessellation $[51,52]$ to determine the nearest neighbors

claim: To identify T1 events robustly against tessellation noise, separations are required to change by at least 5% within a time interval of 1 s.
quote: the separations must change by at least 5% in a time interval of 1 s

claim: T1 clusters are defined as neighboring T1 events with separations less than 6⟨r⟩ occurring while D_G(t) drops monotonically, and analysis focuses on the largest cluster in each global deformation release.
quote: clusters of neighboring T1 events with separations less than $6\langle r\rangle$

claim: Dry 2D foam analysis techniques that determine elastic stresses from polygonal bubble shapes cannot be extended to wetter foams or emulsions (φ < 1).
quote: those analysis techniques cannot be extended to wetter foams or emulsions

claim: At these slow flow rates and high area fractions, all viscous forces are an order of magnitude smaller than the repulsive droplet-droplet contact forces, so D mainly arises from contacts with other droplets.
quote: an order of magnitude smaller than the repulsive droplet-droplet contact forces

claim: Prior experiments found foam velocity profiles strongly influenced by confining glass plates and shear localization near moving boundaries; with pump forcing in this flow geometry, no shear localization is observed.
quote: we do not observe shear localization

claim: Noticeable decreases of deformation are seen as far as three droplet diameters away from a T1 event, suggestive of the flow cooperativity length predicted by theory and prior experiments and simulations.
quote: as far as three diameters away, suggestive of the “flow cooperativity length”

claim: For area fraction φ ≈ 0.9, the mean deformation in a quiescent (non-flowing) sample is D0 = 0.06.
quote: the mean value of the deformation in a quiescent sample is $D_{0} = 0.06$

claim: Immediately after a T1 event, droplets feel strong contact forces moving them into their new positions within 2–4 s, with the relaxation of these forces limited by viscosity.
quote: moving them into their new positions within 2–4 s

claim: The time-averaged deformation depends on flux rate A and x position as ⟨D⟩(x) = D0[1 + A/(kv w(x))] with velocity scale kv = 0.81 mm/s, showing the experiment is not in a rate-independent regime.
quote: $k_{v}=0.81~mm/s$ is a velocity scale

claim: The power spectrum of D_G(t) shows a tendency of power-law decay P(ω) ~ ω^-1 at high frequencies, comparable to spectra found in granular flows.
quote: a tendency of power-law decay $P(\omega)\sim \omega^{-1}$ at high frequencies

claim: Large deformation-release events are rare but not as rare as a Gaussian fit predicts, and the distribution is slightly broader than a previous foam experiment which found a Gaussian.
quote: not as rare as would be predicted from the Gaussian fit

claim: The widths of the ΔD_G distributions are 0.048 ± 0.009 across the six experiments, with no systematic dependence on flow rate.
quote: width =0.048 ± 0.009 for the six experiments

claim: When a T1 event happens, the local deformation first builds up to about 1.5⟨D_G⟩ and then drops dramatically after the event.
quote: builds up (deep red $\sim 1.5\langle D_{G} \rangle$ )

claim: After a T1 event the low-deformation region splits into two parts: one around ΔR ≤ ⟨r⟩ corresponding to the converging pair, and another around ΔR = 2⟨r⟩ corresponding to the diverging pair.
quote: around $\Delta R \leqslant \langle r \rangle$ corresponding to the converging

claim: The region where deformation decreases after a T1 event extends along the ΔR axis to a distance up to 5⟨r⟩.
quote: extends along the $\Delta R$ axis to a distance up to $5\langle r\rangle$

claim: The sizes of the largest T1 clusters are fairly small (mean value close to 2) and have no dependence on the flux rate.
quote: fairly small (a mean value close to 2) and have no dependence on the flux rate

claim: In a time-shuffling null test, randomized T1 events form clusters smaller by 0.4 on average (about 1.6 vs 2.0 particles), and cluster sizes like the observed ones occur only 1% of the time in shuffled data, indicating true spatial correlations between T1 events.
quote: found only 1% of the time in the shuffled data

claim: The ratio N_cluster/N_T1 is about 0.5 on average for small events (N_T1 = 2, often spatially uncorrelated), while for larger events (N_T1 ≥ 3) its distribution peaks around 0.8, showing these bursts often cluster spatially.
quote: The peak of the distribution is around 0.8

claim: T1 events tend to occur in small clusters.
quote: a tendency of the T1 events to occur in small clusters

claim: Droplet deformations caused by forces from neighboring droplets are decreased by nearby T1 events, with a spatial dependence related to the local structure.
quote: decreased by nearby T1 events, with a spatial dependence

claim: The time-averaged velocity profile is parabolic but does not go to zero at the edges of the flow chamber, because droplets slip along the wall.
quote: parabolic, but does not go to zero at the edges of the flow chamber

claim: The global mean deformation shows large temporal fluctuations despite steady flow, similar to previous granular and foam experiments.
quote: large deformation fluctuations are observed

claim: Larger changes of the global deformation take longer times τ, with no dependence on the flow rate.
quote: In general, larger changes of $D_{G}$ take longer times

claim: Beyond a background rate, the largest decreases of the global deformation (ΔD_G ≲ −0.2) are connected to a markedly higher rate of T1 events.
quote: largest decreases of the deformation are connected to a higher rate of T1 events

claim: The deformation relaxation after a T1 event is asymmetric between the two droplet pairs, with the diverging droplets relaxing their shape more significantly than the converging droplets.
quote: The relaxation is asymmetric among the two pairs of droplets in the T1 event

claim: Large decreases of the global deformation are correlated with small cascades of local T1 events, in agreement with previous studies of 2D foams.
quote: small cascades of local T1 events in agreement with previous studies of 2D foams

claim: Because some characteristics of flowing dense amorphous materials are independent of their microscopic details, these quasi-2D results may be relevant for flow of three-dimensional amorphous materials.
quote: independent of their microscopic details
